text: Lesson 4's template hardcoded every value. That's fine for one deployment, but Overlook needs at least two environments: a dev environment where changes get tried safely, and a prod environment holding the real patient data nobody wants a mistake landing in directly.

A param block turns names, location, and the admin login into deploy-time inputs. Location gets a default of eastus since it genuinely doesn't vary here, while the server and database names must differ per environment so dev and prod don't collide. The admin password gets a stricter treatment: the at-secure decorator.

At-secure is a specific guarantee, not just a label for a sensitive value. A secure parameter is never written to deployment history, never logged, and never shown in the CLI's own output. Without it, a plain string default would sit in the file in plain text, and Azure's deployment history would record that same plain-text value a second time — exactly the exposure a healthcare company's security mandate exists to prevent.

With parameters in place, the resource definitions never change between dev and prod — only the values supplied at deploy time do. Next lesson actually runs that deployment with the real Azure CLI command.
